title: Customer reservation signal matrix — Q2 2028
body:
Purpose: rolling planning sheet for per-contract reserved capacity with signal-driven allocation rules, soft-vs-hard commitments, and quick reconciliation guidance. This is intended as an operational handoff to capacity ops and account owners for Q2-Q4 2028.

Header (CSV): ContractID,Customer,Region,Reserved_GPUs,GPU_Type,Commit_Type,Priority_SLO_ms,Target_Util_pct,Runway_months,Start,End,Allocation_Signal,Fallback_Pool,Notes

Rows:
CR-1287,Anodyne Health,us-west1,16,A100-80GB,hard,50,70,18,2028-04-01,2029-10-01,steady,shared-burst,"Primary production capacity for inference; soft 2-hour nightly batch window; colocate on rack A2 to meet cross-tenant latency"
CR-1302,BlueCart,eu-west1,8,A100-40GB,soft,80,55,12,2028-05-01,2029-05-01,peak,on-demand,"E-commerce peak windows (09:00-12:00 CET). Allow elastic burst to 24 GPUs for up to 4h/day; chargeback flagged"
CR-1333,MapleAI,asia-east1,24,H100-80GB,hard,40,75,24,2028-03-15,2030-03-15,steady,regional-fallback,"Low-latency enterprise routing; primary in asia-east1 with regional fallback to us-west1 under maintenance"
CR-1349,Scholar Labs,us-east4,4,A100-40GB,soft,120,45,6,2028-06-01,2028-12-01,opportunistic,shared-burst,"Research workloads, tolerant to preemption; mark as reclaimable during infra incidents"
CR-1358,FinVest,eu-central1,32,H100-80GB,hard,30,85,36,2028-01-01,2031-01-01,steady,dedicated-hot,"Top-tier SLA; reserved across two racks and two availability zones; encrypted KMS integration required"

Allocation signal definitions:
- steady: long-lived reservation, route requests preferentially to contract pool; maintain target util +/- 10pct.
- peak: scheduled burst windows; allow controlled autoscale up to defined burst limit; prebooked daily/weekly schedule required.
- opportunistic: allocate when idle capacity available and de-prioritize during contention; suitable for research/batch.

Quick capacity summary (by region):
- us-west1: Reserved 16 GPUs (A100-80GB) active; slack allowance: 4 GPUs for regional fallback.
- us-east4: Reserved 4 GPUs (A100-40GB) opportunistic; flagged reclaimable.
- eu-west1: Reserved 8 GPUs (A100-40GB) with daily peak windows.
- eu-central1: Reserved 32 GPUs (H100-80GB) high-priority, across two AZs.
- asia-east1: Reserved 24 GPUs (H100-80GB) primary for APAC enterprise customers.
Total reserved GPUs: 84.

Utilization and efficiency targets:
- Target blended utilization (contract pools): 65% steady-state.
- Operational utilization target (after preemption buffers): 55% to 75% depending on commit type.
- Conservative runway buffer: keep 10% of reserved GPUs as hot spares for HA and nightly rollouts.

Reconciliation rules / cadence:
- Weekly runbook check (capacity-ops): reconcile actual usage vs target_util_pct; produce SAR (signal-adjust request) if sustained >70% for 3 consecutive days.
- Monthly contract review (AM + infra): validate Start/End dates, burst windows, and any required infra changes (placements, AZ pinning).
- Incident mode: soft-commit pools may be reclaimed automatically; notify account owner + add to incident timeline.

Allocation heuristics and prioritization (operational):
1) Hard commits mapped to dedicated racks/zones first. Pre-emptible allocation only for "opportunistic" commits.
2) For peak signals, the scheduler pre-warms KV caches and pins weights to reduce cold-start latency during burst windows.
3) Regional fallback: only trigger when >5% of pool capacity is degraded or maintenance >30 minutes.

Cost and billing notes:
- Soft commits: billed at 60% of hard rate when used opportunistically; separate line-item for burst hours beyond daily allowance.
- Chargeback: burst and on-demand usage associated to customer is reconciled weekly; unbilled bursts are auto-flagged for AM review.

Open questions / action items:
- [ ] Confirm FinVest AZ pinning and HSM KMS path (owner: Sofia Ramos) — due 2028-04-20.
- [ ] BlueCart: finalize daily peak window calendar entries in scheduler (owner: Ethan Park) — due 2028-04-10.
- [ ] Ops: validate runbook play for reclaiming opportunistic GPUs without violating data isolation (owner: Liam O'Connor) — due 2028-04-15.

Next steps:
- Send to capacity-ops rotation with diff highlighting any Start/End changes.
- Run quick simulation for May 2028 expected peak (simulate +15% load across eu-west1 and asia-east1) and report expected hot-spare shortfall.

Notes on uniqueness: this sheet encodes signal-driven allocation (steady/peak/opportunistic), explicit fallbacks, and reconciliation heuristics rather than just static allocation tables; use as canonical handoff for Q2 operational planning.
